title: Share your Screen and Talk to Gemini: How Young Learners Interact with Multimodal GenAI While Solving Scratch Tasks
abstract: arXiv:2611.21306v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Children using Scratch to learn programming can struggle with text-heavy, lengthy explanations and hints during debugging. Verbal interactions based on screen sharing or camera data may be an interesting alternative for supporting learners. We therefore explore the quality, use, and perceptions of fifth- and sixth-graders' verbal interactions with a GenAI tutor. The goal is to investigate the quality and use of the multimodal GenAI tutor in the given context. First of all, a pilot study of eight tasks conducted without students helped inform the process of the tutor's classroom evaluation. The classroom study was realized after fifth- and sixth-graders had participated in six Scratch classroom lessons. Then 23 students were introduced to the tutor, worked on the eight tasks with the GenAI tutor, and completed a questionnaire. The analysis of the pilot and classroom study shows that the tutor's responses were intelligible and actionable,

translated_title: 分享你的屏幕并与Gemini对话：年轻学习者在解决Scratch任务时如何与多模态生成式AI互动
translated_abstract: 使用Scratch学习编程的儿童在调试过程中可能难以应对大量文字、冗长的解释和提示。基于屏幕共享或摄像头数据的语音交互可能是支持学习者的一种有趣的替代方案。因此，我们探讨了五、六年级学生与生成式AI辅导老师进行语音交互的质量、使用情况和感知。目标是调查多模态生成式AI辅导老师在该情境下的质量和使用情况。首先，一项在没有学生参与的情况下对八个任务进行的试点研究，为该辅导老师的课堂评估流程提供了参考。课堂研究在五、六年级学生参加完六节Scratch课堂课程后开展。随后，23名学生在了解该辅导老师的使用方式后，与生成式AI辅导老师一起完成了八个任务，并填写了问卷。对试点研究和课堂研究的分析表明，该辅导老师的回复清晰易懂且切实可行。
tldr: 该研究通过课堂实验探索五、六年级学生使用基于屏幕共享的多模态生成式AI辅导老师解决Scratch编程任务时的语音交互情况，发现该辅导老师提供的回复清晰易懂且切实可行。
en_tdlr: This classroom study explored how fifth- and sixth-graders verbally interact with a screen-sharing-based multimodal GenAI tutor while solving Scratch programming tasks, finding that the tutor's responses were intelligible and actionable.
